thread:
sara: seeing p99 spike from AMS pop starting ~12:14 UTC, p99 ~1.3s while p50 stays ~120ms :eyes:
infra-bot: [ALERT] ams-pop interface flaps detected on uplink-2 (12:12-12:40 UTC)
miguel: also visible in runtime traces — kernel selection oscillating around 12:14. logs show fallback kernels being chosen intermittently
jon: can you paste the sampling of batch send times? thinking batching heuristics might be backing off and producing more small batches
sara: here's a quick snippet from the logs and a traceroute I ran:
```
[2026-02-18T12:13:58Z] runtime: kernel_selected=avx_scaled
[2026-02-18T12:14:12Z] runtime: kernel_selected=generic_fallback (latency probe=TRUE)
[2026-02-18T12:14:25Z] runtime: kernel_selected=avx_scaled
```
traceroute to 3.122.45.1 (3.122.45.1), 8 hops max:
 1  10.0.0.1  0.4 ms
 2  100.64.0.1  0.8 ms
 3  172.18.1.1  1.2 ms
 4  ams-edge.provider.net  45.1 ms  <-- jump here, then sometimes reroutes
 5  frankfurt-pop.provider.net  72.9 ms

mei: metrics show KV cache hitrate for that service dropping from 98% -> 73% at the same window. looks like ~30% of requests got routed to FR pop so they missed local KV shards
miguel: kernel fallback + increased small batches + KV misses = compounding perf hit. flamegraph shows attention kernel time up and lock contention on kv-shard locker
jon: confirmed batch metrics: fraction of batches with size<=2 jumped from 12% -> 46% for affected pods between 12:13-12:30. that increases kernel invocation overhead per token
alex: opened a ticket with provider (TICKET-20260218-AMS-BGP). provider says they saw a BGP flap at 12:10 that caused intermittent re-route to FR POP for ~30m. they applied dampening at 12:40
infra-bot: provider status update: dampening applied, route stabilized at 12:48 UTC
jon: quick mitigation applied: added a short-lived routing preference to pin sessions to ams-primary for existing connections (policy prefer-local-pop, TTL 5m) and bumped KV replication grace window to 30s to avoid immediate misses
deploy-bot: route policy prefer-local-pop applied by alex at 12:48 UTC :white_check_mark:
sara: p99 dropped back to ~180ms by 12:52 UTC. p50 unchanged. keeping watch for next hour
mei: follow-ups suggested: 1) avoid immediate kernel fallback on transient latency blips (add hysteresis), 2) smooth batching backoff (don't drop to tiny batches on short network noise), 3) increase KV cross-pop replication/replication-grace heuristics or add read-replica warming when detecting pop handoffs
miguel: filing 3 tickets now: PERF-kernelelect-hysteresis, PERF-batching-smoother, INFRA-kv-replication-grace. will include timeline and flamegraph dump
sara: thanks all. good catch. postmortem / retro next week? :thumbsup:
jon: +1 on postmortem. also add a monitor for sudden KV hitrate drops correlated with route changes
alex: provider closed ticket as "mitigated at edge" but asked us to keep an eye on routing anomalies. I'll push provider BGP dump to the ticket
sara: closing thread for now, will reopen if we see reoccurrence
